skill.name: fixing-motion-performance
skill.description: Review CSS and JavaScript animations for layout thrashing, paint-heavy effects, scroll-linked motion, layer misuse, and view transition risks.
skill.summary: Find and fix frontend animation jank with practical CSS and JavaScript performance rules.
skill.author: ibelick

content.value_statement: Janky animations hurt usability and make interfaces feel slow. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to find motion bottlenecks and propose focused fixes.
actual_capabilities: Identifies layout thrashing caused by mixed DOM reads and writes.
Recommends transform and opacity instead of layout or paint-heavy properties.
Reviews scroll-linked animation patterns and suggests browser timeline or observer alternatives.
Flags risky blur, filter, layer promotion, and view transition usage.
Provides code-level guidance while staying within the existing animation library.
limitations: Does not run browser profiling or collect runtime traces by itself.
Does not guarantee that every suggested CSS API supports every target browser.
Does not replace manual testing on low-powered devices.
Does not migrate animation libraries unless the user explicitly asks.

use_cases.title: Review release animations
use_cases.description: Review a component before release and catch animation choices that cause layout, paint, or scroll jank.

use_cases.title: Standardize motion feedback
use_cases.description: Turn motion rules into consistent review feedback for shared components and interaction patterns.

use_cases.title: Diagnose stuttering interactions
use_cases.description: Diagnose a stuttering interaction and choose lower-cost motion without removing the product intent.

prompt_templates.title: Basic animation review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you want a quick first pass on one file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for animation performance issues: <file>. List violations, impact, and concrete fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Changed code audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before merging animation changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the changed animation code in <files>. Prioritize layout thrashing, scroll-linked motion, blur, filters, and layer promotion.

prompt_templates.title: Focused refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a known interaction feels slow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this janky interaction using the existing animation library. Keep behavior the same and explain each performance tradeoff.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when choosing between competing motion approaches.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two implementation options for this motion pattern. Recommend the lower-cost approach, browser constraints, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A drawer animation transitions width on a large container.
output: Finding: The drawer animates layout on a large surface, which can force repeated layout work.
Suggested fix: Animate transform on an isolated panel and keep layout size stable.

output_examples.input: A reveal effect updates opacity from a scroll event handler.
output: Finding: Scroll events drive animation state every frame and can compete with scrolling.
Suggested fix: Prefer a browser timeline or IntersectionObserver, then pause work off-screen.

output_examples.input: A modal entrance animates blur across the full page.
output: Finding: Large animated blur can trigger expensive paint work and visible stutter.
Suggested fix: Use opacity and translate first, or keep blur small and short.

best_practices: Batch all layout reads before writes when measuring animated elements.
Prefer transform and opacity for motion on meaningful surfaces.
Validate performance-sensitive motion with browser tools and representative devices.
anti_patterns: Animating width, top, or left continuously on large surfaces.
Running scroll handlers to update animation state every frame.
Leaving will-change on many elements after the interaction ends.

faq.question: Can this skill profile my app?
faq.answer: No. It guides review and fixes, but profiling still requires browser tools and real devices.

faq.question: Does it require a specific framework?
faq.answer: No. It applies to CSS, JavaScript, WAAPI, Motion, GSAP, and similar frontend stacks.

faq.question: Will it remove all animations?
faq.answer: No. It favors lower-cost motion that preserves intent when possible.

faq.question: Can it review scroll animations?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for scroll polling, layout work, and better timeline or observer patterns.

faq.question: Is it safe for existing codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill tells the agent to stay within the existing animation stack unless asked otherwise.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Frontend engineers, design system maintainers, and product designers can use it during implementation or review.
